RFC7296-1.2-1.note: Re-judged 2026-09-30. Descriptive row kept MUST under D-3. Positive TestRFC7296InitialExchangesCarryWhatSection12Names runs production handleSAInitRequest/handleAuthRequest/handleAuthResponse in X.509 mode over all four captured messages: IKE_SA_INIT req/resp carry SA+KE+Nonce, the single accepted proposal is one offered and both SAs hold it; Ni/Nr held crosswise and distinct; both KE name the negotiated group, each side holds the other's public value, equal SK_d; IKE_AUTH req IDi+CERT+AUTH+ESP SA+TSi+TSr, resp IDr+CERT+AUTH+one ESP proposal+TSi+TSr; identities recorded, both Established, initiator holds negotiated TS. Negative TestRFC7296TamperedIKESAInitFailsIKEAuth ('authenticate the previous messages'): one flipped octet in the stored IKE_SA_INIT copy on either side (PSK and X.509) keeps that side off Established while an untouched control establishes; genuine, it fails if AUTH stopped covering the IKE_SA_INIT octets. Encryption clause: TestInitialExchangeEncryptionBoundary +/-. The negotiation, nonce and DH clauses are positive-only here; their refusals are held by their own rows (3.3.6, 2.10, 1.2 KE/3.4). Records: handleSAInitRequest +, verifyRemoteAuth -, observed red.

RFC7296-1.3.3-1.note: initiateIKERekey emits KEi (TestRespondIKERekey) and respondIKERekey refuses a rekey without KE naming KEi; test comment still cites Section 1.3.3 where the sentence is 1.3.2

RFC7296-1.3.3-3.note: Positive: TestRFC7296ChildRekeyRequestCarriesTheOfferNonceAndSelectors decrypts ze's initiateChildRekey request at the peer: exactly one SA, one Ni, one TSi and one TSr with selectors, KEi present with pfs enable and absent with pfs disable (the optional clause both ways). Negative (receive side): TestRFC7296ChildRekeyRequestMissingAPayloadIsRefused removes SA, Ni, TSi or TSr one at a time from a peer request: each refused with errMalformedRequest and INVALID_SYNTAX, nothing installed; the complete request is answered. TestRekeyWithoutTrafficSelectorsIsRefused (moved from 2.9-1) adds the no-TS request refusal and its answered twin.

RFC7296-1.3.3-4.note: TestRFC7296ChildRekeyResponseCarriesTheSelectorsAndMayNarrow: ze's respondChildRekey response announces TSi/TSr equal to the installed scope, and ze as rekey initiator installs an answer narrowed to 10.1.0.0/25 from a /24 proposal (the may-be-a-subset clause). TestChildRekeyAnswerWithoutTrafficSelectorsIsRefused (moved from 2.9-1): a response without TS payloads is refused and installs nothing, the same fixture with both payloads installs their scope.

RFC7296-1.4-1.note: Child SA Delete response carries a Delete naming the paired inbound SPI; IKE SA Delete draws an empty response

RFC7296-1.4.1-4.note: TestDelCrossingDeleteAnswersWithoutAPairedDelete runs the production crossing sequence (recordOwnDelete, send, remove) and asserts the response to the peer's crossing Delete carries no Delete payload; reddens when crossOwnDelete stops detecting the crossing. TestDelWithoutOwnDeleteTheSameRequestIsPaired pins the row's own 'In that case' scope: outside the exception the same Delete draws the paired Delete §1.4.1 requires ('Normally, the response ... will contain Delete payloads for the paired SAs'), so a responder that never pairs cannot pass. The tags on TestLcyInformationalResponseCarriesNoDeletePayload are gone and its stale premise rewritten.

RFC7296-1.7-2.note: HMAC PRFs accept 1..200-octet keys and consume the key

RFC7296-2.10-2.note: Clause (subject 'Nonces used in IKEv2', §2.10): at least 128 bits, both directions. Send: TestRFC7296EmittedNoncesAreAtLeast128Bits checks all six nonces ze emits (IKE_SA_INIT Ni/Nr, Child SA rekey Ni/Nr, IKE SA rekey Ni/Nr, rekeys decrypted off the wire) are >= 16 octets. Receive: TestNonceLengthBounds accepts 16 and refuses 15 octets with ErrNonceTooShort, the genuine receiving-side negative (R1a). Row text is a subject-less fragment of the §2.10 sentence ('MUST be at least 128 bits in size'); a D-10 row correction to the full sentence span is owed by the author, not a verdict matter.

RFC7296-2.10-3.note: Positive reads the PRF list from the registry and asserts every emission site: IKE_SA_INIT Ni and Nr, Child SA rekey Ni and Nr, IKE SA rekey Ni and Nr, the four rekey nonces decrypted off the wire by the other side. Negative is R1(b): an IKE SA rekey that negotiates prf-hmac-sha2-512 (checked on the replacement SA's Proposal.PRF, half 32 > the 16-octet wire minimum), and its Ni and Nr off the wire each meet half that key. A per-site shortening at any of the six sites reddens the positive. The IKE_SA_INIT nonces are read from SA.LocalNonce, not the wire.

RFC7296-2.11-2.note: TestRFC7296ReplyLandsOnTheRequestSourcePort reads the reply datagram on the socket bound to the request's odd source port (response flag, request Message ID, decrypts under the IKE SA). The negative is now TestRFC7296ReplyDoesNotGoToTheConfiguredEndpoint alone: the configured remote, the violating destination, receives nothing. The NAT-T unauthenticated-packet unit moved to RFC7296-2.23-13, the row it proves. The older natt positive asserts only the stored endpoint and is supplementary.

RFC7296-2.13-2.note: the tags assert SK_* key sizing, which is RFC7296-2.13-3; no supported cipher has invalid key values (AES only), so nothing tests this row's rule. no supported transform has invalid key values (encryptionRegistry is AES CBC/GCM/CCM only, no DES/3DES); the tags assert SK_* key sizing, which is RFC7296-2.13-3

RFC7296-2.15-2.note: The weak finding (use path unexercised) is closed. Parse side: ipsec TestPSKHasNoNullTerminatorAdded (parseAuthConfig keeps the PSK octets, adds and strips nothing). Use side, new engine/rfc7296_psk_terminator_test.go: positive TestRFC7296PSKIsUsedWithoutANullTerminator compares computePSKAuth's AUTH with an independent stdlib HMAC-SHA2-256 prf(prf(secret,'Key Pad for IKEv2'),SignedOctets) over the secret octets alone (equal) and over secret+0x00 (not equal), and verifyPSKAuth accepts the no-terminator AUTH; negative TestRFC7296PSKWithANullTerminatorAddedIsRefused: verifyPSKAuth refuses the AUTH over secret+0x00 with errAuthFailed, so the receiving side adds no terminator either. Producers read: both pass []byte(sa.PeerCfg.Auth.PSK) to computeAuthFromSharedSecret/verifyAuthFromSharedSecret. Records: computePSKAuth and verifyPSKAuth panic reverts observed red. Judge ran both: PASS. Prose defect, not a proof gap: psktermSecret is 65 octets, while its comment and both claims say 64; the claim wording should be corrected (and the records re-recorded) by the author.

RFC7296-2.16-11.note: EAP responder AUTH is an RFC 7427 signature verified under the cert key; no-cert EAP refused at setup and config; initiator refuses PSK AUTH from EAP responder; PSK peers unaffected

RFC7296-2.16-16.note: Non-compliant behaviour: an IKEv2 exchange selecting an EAP method that establishes no key when the operator did not name one. Positive: TestRFC3748IKEv2EAPModesSelectAKeyDerivingMethod fails ('auth mode %s selected an EAP method that derives no key') for any EAP mode other than AuthEAPMD5 whose newEAPSession session answers false to DerivesKey. Negative: TestRFC3748IKEv2NoAuthModeSelectsAKeylessMethod sweeps every AuthMode value through newEAPSession and startEAPExchange, and assertKeylessModeIsNamedAndAnnounced goes red when a keyless method is reached by an unnamed value or without the adoption warning. The SHOULD NOT is met as a deviation the operator must name, which the warning makes visible.

RFC7296-2.17-1.note: DeriveChildSAKeys slices recomputed prf+ KEYMAT with both initiator keys before responder keys

RFC7296-2.17-2.note: encryption key then integrity key per direction, positional, asserted against recomputed KEYMAT

RFC7296-2.18-3.note: TestPropDHNoneRefusedForIKESA covers the responder refusing DH NONE in NegotiateIKE; the initiator half (MUST NOT propose NONE when rekeying) and the rekey context are not asserted

RFC7296-2.2-3.note: finishResponderEstablish advances only the inbound counter; responder's first request id 0 is classified as new by the initiator

RFC7296-2.20-1.note: Section 2.20's method: TestRFC7296InformationalVersionRequestDrawsNoCP sends the product INFORMATIONAL handler (handleInformationalOwned, MOBIKE enabled so mobikeResponsePayloads builds the answer) a post-auth CP(CFG_REQUEST, empty APPLICATION_VERSION) and asserts the response the peer decrypts carries no CP; TestRFC7296InformationalVersionRequestReflectsNoVersionString pushes toward reflection with a non-empty version string and asserts no CP and no non-empty APPLICATION_VERSION. IKE_AUTH path: TestRFC7296ResponderAnswersAVersionRequestWithNoCP. Sweep: TestZeDeclinesApplicationVersion. Ze supports no CP, so the no-CP arm is the one that binds.

RFC7296-2.21.2-1.note: Re-judged 2026-09-30 (independent judge). Both halves asserted. Unsupported critical payload: rfc7296_inner_error_answers_test.go::TestRFC7296UnsupportedCriticalPayloadDrawsOnlyThatNotify sends a protected INFORMATIONAL whose only inner payload is private type 200 with C=1; the request never reaches the exchange handlers (peerAlive false) and the answer, decrypted under the IKE SA, carries exactly one payload, UNSUPPORTED_CRITICAL_PAYLOAD with data {200}. Malformed message: TestErrInnerParseFailureDrawsInvalidSyntaxAndOuterDrawsNothing (truncated inner chain answered with INVALID_SYNTAX only). Negative: TestCritChainReportsTruncationButNotBadContents (bad payload contents are not a malformed message). Revert record observed red on inbound.go::respondInnerParseError.

RFC7296-2.21.2-2.note: initiator establishes despite piggybacked error notify; AUTHENTICATION_FAILED still kills the SA

RFC7296-2.21.4-2.note: INVALID_IKE_SPI answer copies SPIs, Message ID and exchange type with Response flag, per request; answered over the arrival socket framing; .ci covers arrival socket

RFC7296-2.21.4-4.note: answer holds exactly one INVALID_IKE_SPI Notify with empty SPI and data

RFC7296-2.21.4-6.note: unprotected notify leaves state, counters, child SA and DPD timer untouched; same notify protected reaches handlers

RFC7296-2.21.4-7.note: Re-judged 2026-09-30 (independent judge) after the row was narrowed to the MUST NOT sentence, verbatim at RFC 7296 Section 2.21.4: "The recipient MUST NOT change the state of any SAs as a result, but may wish to audit the event to aid in diagnosing malfunctions." The SHOULD-send sentence is RFC7296-2.21.4-8 {gap}. TestErrProtectedInformationalNotifyChangesNoState: a protected INFORMATIONAL carrying INVALID_SELECTORS (the kind of notify a node sends after a suspicious ESP packet) is answered, leaves the IKE SA state unchanged and the Child SA in place; control: the same exchange carrying a Delete does change state. Revert records observed red on inbound.go::handleInformationalOwned. Limit: the Child SA check is pointer identity, so an in-place mutation of the Child SA would not be seen; handleInformationalOwned acts on Delete and MOBIKE notifies only.
RFC7296-2.21.4-7.upgrade_reason: The earlier weak verdict rested only on the SHOULD-send clause the row then carried. The row now quotes the MUST NOT sentence alone (Correction 2026-09-30), the send clause moved to RFC7296-2.21.4-8, and the unchanged unit asserts exactly the narrowed obligation, re-read here against Section 2.21.4 and handleInformationalOwned.

RFC7296-2.21.4-8.note: Judged 2026-09-30 at the producers. A message outside any known IKE SA goes to answerOutOfSA (notify_error.go), which answers an unprotected INVALID_IKE_SPI from the header alone and never looks up an IKE SA held with the sender's address; an unprotected message at a cached Message ID of an existing SA is dropped and counted in handleOwnedInbound (inbound.go, unprotected-retransmit). Neither path initiates an INFORMATIONAL exchange over the existing SA. The one protected emission Ze raises unprompted, INVALID_MESSAGE_ID (sendInvalidMessageID), answers an authenticated in-SA request under Section 2.3 and is not this sentence's suspicious message.

RFC7296-2.23-1.note: TestNATDetectionPresent/Absent call DetectNAT on hand-built hashes; no tagged unit shows the initiator checks the received NAT_DETECTION payloads during IKE_SA_INIT, so the tests stay green if the engine stopped calling DetectNAT

RFC7296-2.23-10.note: every Child SA accepts both ESP forms inbound (AcceptBothESPForms) and both forms are programmable; kernel behavior measured by the cited QEMU tests

RFC7296-2.23-12.note: Second sentence enforced: TestNonESPMarker fails ('StripNonESPMarker returned false for valid IKE packet') when a zero-marked packet is not recognised as IKE, and TestNonESPMarkerESPPacket fails ('ESP packet should not be recognized as IKE') when a non-zero SPI is taken for IKE. First sentence unproven: no tagged unit asserts that a UDP-encapsulated ESP packet Ze sends carries the ESP header immediately after the UDP header (the kernel XFRM encapsulation Ze configures).

RFC7296-2.23-13.note: Row is verbatim §2.23. Positive TestRFC7296ValidatedPacketFromANewEndpointMovesTheSA: responder not behind a NAT and without MOBIKE; a second validated request from a new port moves peerEndpoint and remoteUDPAddr (what every send and retransmission reads), and the response is read on the new socket. Negatives each violate one bound of the sentence against adoptAuthenticatedEndpoint: behind a NAT (§2.23 'A host behind a NAT SHOULD NOT do this type of dynamic address update') and MOBIKE keep the stored endpoint (TestRFC7296ValidatedPacketDoesNotMoveTheSAOutsideTheRow); a packet with an in-window Message ID whose integrity check fails, from a new endpoint, moves nothing (TestNattUnauthenticatedPacketDoesNotMoveTheEndpoint). Each guard in the producer has a case that reddens without it. The 'new packet' replay bound is a separate lowercase-should sentence, not this row.

RFC7296-2.23-2.note: Row now quotes the §2.23 ESP sentence (verbatim). Positive TestChildSANATTEncapPorts is sound: NATDetected makes both Child SAs UDP-encapsulated on 4500. Negative TestChildSANoNATNoEncap is only an antecedent guard: without a NAT §2.23 lets either side choose ('Either side can decide whether or not to use UDP encapsulation for ESP'), so always-encapsulate complies and the negative asserts ze's interop choice, not this row. Only createFirstChildSA is driven; a rekeyed ESP SA under NAT is not asserted. No refusal path exists for a genuine negative (R1 fallback).

RFC7296-2.23-3.note: Re-read 2026-09-27 after the RFC3948-2.2-1 tags were deleted and the RFC3948-2.1-3 tags moved to RFC7296-2.23-12 in these units (comment lines only; bodies unchanged). Forbidden behaviour: an IKE message sent on UDP port 4500 without the four zero octets prepended, or not immediately after the UDP header. TestNonESPMarker exercises AddNonESPMarker/StripNonESPMarker in isolation and TestNonESPMarkerESPPacket shows a non-zero SPI is not stripped; no tagged unit shows an IKE message Ze sends on port 4500 carries the four zero octets

RFC7296-2.24-1.note: installed Child SAs are tunnel mode with no ECN-disabling field (engine and XFRM scans); VPP InstallSA sets ENCAP/DECAP_COPY_ECN. Negatives are non-vacuity checks rather than violating inputs

RFC7296-2.24-2.note: same units: XFRM state carries no NOECN path, VPP sets DECAP_COPY_ECN; transport mode refused by VPP backend

RFC7296-2.4-1.note: empty INFORMATIONAL request answered by an encrypted INFORMATIONAL response with zero inner payloads echoing the message ID; a response is not answered

RFC7296-2.4-2.note: No test carries an RFC requirement: RFC7296-2.4-2 tag; the only mentions are prose in plan/immediate/spec-ike-dpd-demand-driven.md, so nothing can go red on non-compliance and the row is unproven. The behaviour exists: newDPDState (internal/component/ike/engine/dpd.go) arms a periodic empty-INFORMATIONAL probe for every peer, the YANG dead-peer-detection interval defaulting to 30 seconds with range 1..3600, so an IKE SA that has received nothing protected recently is still checked. Owed: a tagged unit in both polarities (probe sent when no protected message arrived within the interval; none while a probe is outstanding), which the demand-driven DPD spec already plans.

RFC7296-2.4-3.note: Re-judged 2026-09-30. Unprotected-message clause unchanged: TestRteUnownedEstablishedSATrustsNothing (cleartext Delete/CREATE_CHILD_SA refused, authenticated Delete still ends the SA) and the two responder IKE_SA_INIT units. Routing-information clause now asserted with real loopback ICMP (linux, unprivileged, ran and passed, not skipped): the IKE socket sets IP_RECVERR and the queued Port Unreachable is consumed by the transport's real error-queue path (records: panic in drainErrorQueue + and deliverQueuedError - observed red, so the ICMP path runs in each unit). Negative TestRFC7296ICMPFromThePeerWhileWaitingFailsNothing: a Port Unreachable from the peer's own address:port while a probe waits, plus a Fragmentation Needed routed into handleSizeRefusal (the engine's only ICMP consumer): SA stays Established, probe stays outstanding with no sa-failed answer, nothing reaches Refusals, later authenticated answer settles it. Positive TestRFC7296ICMPUnreachableDoesNotFailTheSA: after a queued Port Unreachable the SA's next request reaches the peer and the peer's authenticated answer settles the probe as fits. Limit: the assertion covers today's consumers (Refusals channel, handleSizeRefusal); a new ICMP consumer outside them would need its own test.

RFC7296-2.4-4.note: Re-read 2026-09-27. Forbidden: INITIAL_CONTACT sent outside the first IKE_AUTH. TestInitiatorEmitsInitialContact fails if the responder did not parse it from the first IKE_AUTH; TestInitialContactAbsentFromRekey fails if an IKE rekey CREATE_CHILD_SA carries it. buildAuthRequest (auth.go) is the only producer of NotifyInitialContact, so no other exchange can carry it.

RFC7296-2.5-13.note: Nonce/KE/SA order parses with all three; engine handleAuthResponse accepts unconventional order

RFC7296-2.5-18.note: Response side now proven through the real handler: protected INFORMATIONAL requests with an unrecognized critical inner payload (types 200 and 49) draw a response with exactly one notify, UNSUPPORTED_CRITICAL_PAYLOAD, whose Notification Data is the one octet of that type (so the data follows the payload, not a constant). Negative: the same payload with the critical bit clear is answered with no such notify. Wire tags keep the parse error carrying the type and the non-critical demotion.

RFC7296-2.5-7.note: Every RESERVED field of a payload body Ze decodes is now covered: AUTH 1-3, KE 2-3, ID 1-3, TS 1-3, CP 1-3, Proposal 1, Transform 1 and 5 set to 0xff decode without error to the DeepEqual value of the zero body (encoder checked to send them zero); generic payload header flags and the CP attribute R bit keep their HEAD tags. Negative (control against a decoder that ignores everything): the adjacent defined octet at 0xff changes the decode or is refused. Payloads with no RESERVED field (Notify, Delete, Nonce, CERT, EAP, SK) have nothing to ignore; the IKE header X flag bits are §3.1's row. Row text is the pronoun fragment 'their content ...' whose subject is 2.5-6's; a D-10 row correction is owed by the author.

RFC7296-2.5-8.note: undefined payload type decoded as payloadRaw and the chain continues, outer and inner chain; defined type not demoted

RFC7296-2.6-1.note: D-8 fixed: SATable.lookupInbound (called by both receive loops, dispatchInbound and dispatchNATTInbound) maps a packet by its full SPI pair; one half decides only on a zero SPI (retransmitted IKE_SA_INIT request by initiator SPI; IKE_SA_INIT response to the half-open (i,0) SA, which also keeps the non-zero-responder-SPI INVALID_KE/COOKIE response reachable, sa_init_retry resets the key). Positive: two SAs sharing an initiator SPI each reached by their own pair, response reaches the half-open SA, zero-rSPI retransmit reaches the responder SA. Negative: (shared, stranger) and (stranger, first) map to no SA; the pre-fix fallback fails it. Wire header tags keep the SPI pair round-trip and short-header refusal. Residual: the tests call lookupInbound directly, not the receive loops, so a fallback re-added in register.go itself would stay green.

RFC7296-2.7-1.note: NegotiateIKE picks one proposal or returns ErrNoProposalChosen; TestEsnResponderAnswersOnlyAValueTheOfferCarried asserts SAr2 carries one proposal with exactly one transform of the type and maps refusal to NO_PROPOSAL_CHOSEN

RFC7296-2.8-2.note: no lifetime transform or attribute reaches the wire (TestLifetimesNotNegotiatedOnWire); lifetime state derives from the local value (TestSALifetimeTime)

RFC7296-2.9-1.note: narrowChildSelectors answers a disjoint proposal with TS_UNACCEPTABLE and records no pairs, and accepts an overlapping one narrowed (TestTSUnacceptableIsSentWhenNothingIsAcceptable); the rekey initiator installs an answer inside its proposal and refuses a wider one (TestChildRekeyInitiatorInstallsTheAnsweredSelectors). The two TS-presence units formerly tagged here moved to RFC7296-1.3.3-3 and 1.3.3-4.

RFC7296-3.1-11.note: V bit clear on every built message; set V bit on receipt changes nothing

RFC7296-3.1-12.note: TestNrsResponseNeverDrawsAResponse drives the responder handshake, out-of-SA admission (with a matching source so the flag is the only difference), INFORMATIONAL and CREATE_CHILD_SA paths: a message marked as a response builds and sends nothing, the same message with the flag clear is answered. TestNrsInformationalHandlerRefusesAResponse takes handleInformationalOwned at its own entry point, both ways. TestResponseBitMatchesDirection's moved negative repeats the handshake arm (R-set IKE_SA_INIT leaves the responder idle, the clear one reaches sa-init-received). The Section 2.21.2 exception is not exercised here.

RFC7296-3.1-13.note: Every call site of initiatorFlag is now product-driven for both original roles: IKE_SA_INIT/IKE_AUTH request and response, INFORMATIONAL responses, IKE rekey request, DPD probes (earlier units), and TestRFC7296InitiatorBitAtEveryRemainingCallSite: writeDelete and sendIKESATeardown Delete requests and startMobikeRequest read off the peer socket, respondMobikeError, buildErrorNotifyResponse, initiateChildRekey, respondChildRekey accepted and INVALID_KE, respondIKERekey accepted and INVALID_KE. Each check asserts I == original-initiator and the R flag, so a site deriving I from direction goes red on a response or on the original responder's request, and a hard-coded value goes red for one role. The older unit's test-built Delete remains but no longer carries the Delete claim alone.

RFC7296-3.1-2.note: IKE_AUTH request and response inner chains hold no SK payload; negative is a vacuity guard

RFC7296-3.1-3.note: Send: GenerateSPI and new SAs asserted non-zero (TestSPIZeroRules). Receive, both dispatchers: TestRFC7296ZeroInitiatorSPIIsDroppedOnReceipt (port 500, dispatchInbound) and TestRFC7296ZeroInitiatorSPIIsDroppedOnTheNATTSocket (port 4500, dispatchNATTInbound, non-ESP marker) each put an SA with a zero Initiator's SPI in the table, so without the guard the zero-iSPI datagram would reach that SA's owner; the following non-zero datagram is delivered (NAT-T: marker stripped). Records are whole-producer reverts (reach); the isolation comes from the zero-iSPI SA in the table.

RFC7296-3.1-4.note: First message: TestSPIZeroRules asserts octets 8..15 zero in Ze's IKE_SA_INIT request, non-zero in the response. Cookie repeat: TestRFC7296ResponderSPIIsZeroInTheFirstMessageAndItsCookieRepeat answers a COOKIE challenge whose Responder's SPI is 0909..09, checks the repeat carries the COOKIE notify and the same Initiator's SPI, and asserts octets 8..15 of the repeat are zero, red on a retry that copies the challenge's SPI.

RFC7296-3.1-7.note: every engine-built message has X bits clear; I and R observed so the mask is not vacuous

RFC7296-3.1-8.note: IKE_SA_INIT with all X bits set is processed as the clean one; R bit set changes treatment

RFC7296-3.1-9.note: Positive: TestResponseBitMatchesDirection asserts the exact R bit on every engine-built request and response. Negative (ruling R1 a, receive side): TestRFC7296InitiatorIgnoresAResponseWithTheRBitClear feeds the initiator's handleInbound the responder's real IKE_SA_INIT answer with only the R bit cleared (stays StateSAInitSent), then the untouched answer (advances), so the refusal is the R bit's doing. The old responder-side negative moved to RFC7296-3.1-12, which it proves. Record: whole-producer revert of fsm.go::handleInbound (reach); isolation by the one-bit difference.

RFC7296-3.10-3.note: Producer side now proven: every notify of the IKE_SA_INIT request ze builds and the UNSUPPORTED_CRITICAL_PAYLOAD error answer ze sends, decoded off the wire, carry SPI Size 0 and no SPI octets (error data exactly one octet). Negative (R1b): an IKE-SA notify struct naming Protocol ID 1 and SPI Size 8 with no SPI octets is still encoded with SPI Size 0 and an empty SPI field. RFC7296-3.10.1-3.note: Re-judged 2026-09-30 (independent judge). INVALID_SYNTAX for errors no other status type covers, in an authenticated request: truncated inner chain (TestErrInnerParseFailureDrawsInvalidSyntaxAndOuterDrawsNothing) and now Payload Length 0 and 3 (rfc7296_inner_error_answers_test.go::TestRFC7296UncoveredInnerErrorsDrawInvalidSyntax), each answered with exactly one notify, INVALID_SYNTAX, and not dispatched. Every non-critical inner-chain parse error reaches the same single producer, respondInnerParseError, which answers INVALID_SYNTAX unconditionally. An invalid field value (a Delete with the wrong SPI Size) is answered with INVALID_SYNTAX under RFC7296-3.11-2's tests. Negative: an outer parse failure (Message ID and checksum never validated) draws nothing. Revert record observed red on inbound.go::respondInnerParseError.

Each case reddens under the break of its own deleteMalformed arm. TestRFC7296DeleteSPISizeFixedForItsProtocolIsAccepted: IKE 0 and AH 4 draw no notify, so the refusal is per-protocol size and not a refusal of IKE/AH Deletes. Negative (ruling R1 b, no refusal path exists): TestRFC7296RecipientAcceptsAnIVTheSenderShouldNotHaveChosen decrypts a message reusing the previous IV and one whose IV is the previous message's final ciphertext block, the IVs a recipient that policed the sender's rule would refuse; such a break leaves the positive green and turns this unit red. The checksum-corruption negative moved to RFC7296-3.14-6. The row is still the fragment "recipients MUST accept any value".

RFC7296-3.14-6.note: Checksum over the encrypted message. Positive (TestRFC7296ChecksumIsTheHMACOfTheEncryptedMessage): the ICV Ze writes equals HMAC-SHA2-256-128 under SK_ai computed with crypto/hmac outside Ze over header, SK header, IV and ciphertext, and the peer accepts it. Negative (TestRFC7296ChecksumOverThePlaintextIsRefused): the ICV recomputed over header, IV and the plaintext (decrypted outside Ze) is refused by decryptAndParse, while the same construction over the ciphertext is accepted, so only the MAC input differs. Records: positive revert of engine/auth.go::buildSKMessageCBCWithMsgID, negative revert of crypto/cipher.go::VerifyIntegrity. CBC only: an AEAD transform carries no separate Integrity Checksum Data. The older round-trip and octet-flip units stay tagged and add nothing to discrimination.

RFC7296-3.3.2-1.note: Row quotes the Section 3.3.3 span: the understand-all-types sentence and the IKE line (ENCR, PRF, INTEG*, D-H). IKE line through the responder's selection (wireProposalsToIKE + crypto.NegotiateIKE): a complete proposal is chosen and an AES-GCM proposal without INTEG is chosen with integrity NONE (TestRFC7296PeerIKEProposalWithTheMandatoryTypesIsAccepted); proposals missing ENCR or INTEG draw ErrProposalIncomplete and one missing D-H draws ErrDHGroupNone (TestRFC7296PeerIKEProposalMissingAMandatoryTypeIsRefused); missing PRF draws ErrNoProposalChosen (TestIKEWireProposalHasAllTransforms). TestResponderRequiresKEForDH proves the KE payload, a neighbour. Re-judged 2026-09-30 (leftovers): the weak finding (understand-every-type clause unproven under this id) is closed by tagging TestTftUnknownTransformTypeMakesProposalUnacceptable: positive, a wire IKE proposal of ENCR, PRF, INTEG and D-H is converted and accepted, so every IKE-line type is understood (an ununderstood one would mark the proposal unacceptable); negative, the same proposal plus an unassigned type 6 or an ESN transform is refused with ErrNoProposalChosen, which shows the understood predicate is what admits the four. The negative is the table-bound side (shared with RFC7296-3.3.3-1 and 3.3.6-4); the missing-type negatives above remain this row's direct violations. Records: TransformTypeUnderstoodIKE panic revert observed red both polarities. Judge ran the unit: PASS.

RFC7296-3.3.3-1.note: transformTypeUnderstood per protocol matches the Section 3.3.3 table; engine refuses ESN in an IKE proposal. Re-judged 2026-09-30 (leftovers): TestTftUnknownTransformTypeMakesProposalUnacceptable changed only by the two added RFC7296-3.3.2-1 tag lines; body identical to HEAD, judge ran it: PASS; verdict unchanged.

RFC7296-3.3.5-5.note: Clauses: for such transforms the Key Length attribute MUST always be included (sender); proposals not containing it MUST be rejected (receiver). The receiver clause is asserted (AES-CBC and AES-CTR offers without Key Length refused with ErrKeyLengthMissing, accepted with it). The sender clause has no assertion: no Ze-built proposal is checked for a Key Length attribute on AES-CBC/CTR.

RFC7296-3.3.6-5.note: Judged 2026-09-30 at the producers after the D-8 fix: wire Transform.AttrsUnderstood (attrFormats, Key Length only); appendIKECombinations and espProposalMatches drop a transform carrying an unknown attribute and keep its siblings, and refuse the proposal only when an offered type loses every transform (IKEProposal.UnacceptableTransformType -> ErrTransformUnacceptable in ikeProposalComplete; ESP offered!=usable). This matches Section 3.3.6: the transform is unacceptable, other transforms of the same type are processed as usual, and a type with nothing acceptable leaves no complete set to select. Negative TestRFC7296UnacceptableTransformAloneRefusesTheProposal: unknown ENCR id alone, and each IKE type (ENCR/PRF/INTEG/D-H) and ESP type (ENCR/INTEG/ESN) carrying attribute 99 alone is refused, with a per-type control without the attribute accepted, so the attribute is the only difference (isolated); this failed before the fix. Positive TestRFC7296UnacceptableTransformLeavesSiblingsOnOffer: the unknown-id and unknown-attribute transform beside an understood sibling, both orders, IKE accepted with the sibling's ENCR and ESP matched (catches an over-reaction that refuses the type or proposal). ESP response is built from config, so no unacceptable attribute is echoed. HEAD crypto/engine tags remain supplementary. Records: appendIKECombinations +, espProposalMatches -, observed red.

RFC7296-3.5-3.note: Re-read 2026-09-27. Forbidden: refusing ID_IPV4_ADDR, ID_FQDN, ID_RFC822_ADDR or ID_KEY_ID under configuration. TestRemoteIDAcceptsEveryMandatoryType fails if checkRemoteIdentity refuses any of the four with a matching remote-id, and (anti-vacuity) if it accepts a wrong one. TestRemoteIDRefusesTypesItCannotCompare shows acceptance is per-type; its comment names ID_DER_ASN1_DN as refused but the body tests only ID_DER_ASN1_GN (stale comment).

RFC7296-3.5-5.note: Row now quotes the ID_FQDN entry through its ban (verbatim §3.5; the keyword-free ASCII/IDNA sentence the old weak verdict turned on is out of the span). TestWp2IDTerminatorRefused: a peer ID_FQDN holding NUL, CR or LF is refused by refuseIDTerminators, and ze's own local-id/remote-id holding one is refused by ValidateIdentities (config.go:158), the only path to the ID_FQDN ze sends (encodeIKEID). TestWp2IDWithoutTerminatorAccepted: clean FQDN accepted on both paths, NUL ID_KEY_ID left alone, so neither check refuses everything. Both halves call the validators directly; the call sites remote_id.go:393 and config.go:158 are unasserted. Producer comments at remote_id.go:352 and ipsec/validate.go:181 still quote the invented sentence the row dropped.

RFC7296-3.5-6.note: Row is verbatim §3.5 (ID_RFC822_ADDR entry through its ban). The ban binds whoever sends an ID_RFC822_ADDR, and ze never sends one: encodeIKEID emits only ID_IPV4_ADDR, ID_IPV6_ADDR or ID_FQDN. The tags prove a receive-side refusal (refuseIDTerminators refuses a peer's NUL mail address; a clean one is accepted, and a clean mail remote-id commits), which §3.5 does not require. No tagged unit can fail on a violation Ze could commit; route per R2 (move the tags or retire the row as binding the ID_RFC822_ADDR sender).

Send half unchanged: TestChuBothHashAndURLFormatsAreConfigurable fails unless buildCertPayloads emits encodings 12 and 13 with the SHA-1 and URL. Accept half now asserted: rfc7296_hash_url_accept_test.go::TestRFC7296ReceivedHashAndURLFormatsAreAcceptedWhenConfigured, hash-and-url ON, receives encoding 12 (leaf DER) and encoding 13 (DER bundle leaf+intermediate) with http URLs on a loopback server; acceptedCertEncoding admits each, storeRemoteCerts fetches (server hit), matches the SHA-1, stores the leaf as the peer cert and the bundle's intermediate in the chain.
